units.source_text: 萤兵部卿亲王推想今夜六条院内照例必有管弦之会，便驱车来访。

en.t: Prince Hotaru, Minister of War, supposed that there would as usual be a gathering of music at the Rokujo estate that night, and came calling by carriage.

units.source_text: 夕雾大将也带了身份相当的殿上人来了。

en.t: General Yugiri also came, bringing court gentlemen of suitable rank with him.

units.source_text: 他们随着琴声寻访，知道源氏在三公主处，便立刻找到了。

en.t: Following the sound of the koto as they searched, they learned that Genji was with the Third Princess and found him at once.

units.source_text: 源氏说道：“今天寂寞得很。

en.t: Genji said, "It has been very lonely today.

units.source_text: 不曾准备管弦之会，然而很想听听久已不闻的美妙之音，所以独自在这里弹琴。

en.t: I had made no preparations for a musical gathering, but I longed to hear those beautiful sounds I had not heard for so long, and so I was playing here alone.
You have come at just the right time."

units.source_text: 就在这里添设座位，请亲王入座。

en.t: Seats were added there on the spot, and the prince was invited to sit down.

units.source_text: 今夜宫中本当召开赏月宴会，后来作罢了，大家觉得扫兴。

en.t: That night a moon-viewing banquet was supposed to be held at court, but it had later been canceled, leaving everyone disappointed.

units.source_text: 诸王侯公卿传闻萤兵部卿亲王等已赴六条院，便都来了。

en.t: When the princes, nobles, and high courtiers heard that Prince Hotaru and the others had gone to the Rokujo estate, they all came as well.

units.source_text: 于是相与听赏虫声，评定优劣，又演奏种种琴筝。

en.t: Then they listened together to the insects' voices, judged which were finest, and played various kotos and zithers.

units.source_text: 逸兴正浓之时，源氏说道：“有月之夜，不论何时，无不令人感慨。

en.t: When the pleasure of the evening was at its height, Genji said, "A moonlit night, whenever it comes, always stirs deep feelings.

units.source_text: 就中今宵清光皎洁的月色，尤其使人神往世外，百感交集。

en.t: Above all, tonight's clear and brilliant moonlight draws the heart beyond this world and brings countless emotions together.

units.source_text: 柏木权大纳言不幸身亡，教人每逢兴会，怀念不置。

en.t: Since Kashiwagi, the Provisional Grand Counselor, sadly passed away, every delightful gathering makes one remember him without cease.

units.source_text: 少了此人，似觉公私万事都失却了光彩。

en.t: Without him, it feels as though everything in both public and private life has lost its brightness.

units.source_text: 此人最能理解花容鸟语之情趣，真是一个颇有见识的话伴，可惜……”

en.t: He understood better than anyone the charm of flowers' beauty and birds' songs, and he was truly a discerning companion in conversation; what a loss..."

units.source_text: 听了自己弹出的琴声，也不胜悲戚，双泪沾袖。

en.t: Hearing the sound of the koto he himself was playing, he too could not bear his grief, and tears from both eyes wet his sleeves.

units.source_text: 他猜想帘内的三公主亦必听到这话，不免心生妒恨。

en.t: He imagined that the Third Princess behind the curtains must also have heard these words, and he could not help feeling jealousy and resentment.

units.source_text: 然而，在此种游宴之际，他总是首先恋念柏木，皇上等也都怀念此人。

en.t: Yet on occasions of revelry like this, he always thought first and fondly of Kashiwagi, and the emperor and the others all remembered him too.

units.source_text: 他就对诸人说：“今夜我们就来开个欣赏铃虫的宴会，痛饮达旦吧。”

en.t: So he said to everyone, "Tonight let us hold a banquet to enjoy the bell crickets, and drink heartily until dawn."
